status: Draft. Owners and times are a strawman from general practice, not yet reviewed by an SME.

template.label: Template
template.note: Fixed wording from this template; the same on every block until an SME edits it.

funding.label: Funding agent
funding.note: FundingAgent's approved funding matches for this recommendation.

zoning.label: Zoning lookup
zoning.note: The zones fronting the block from the county zoning map, checked against the Zoning Ordinance's use tables (§27-5101). A lookup, not a model: every finding cites its source.

policy.label: Policy agent
policy.note: PolicyAgent (supporting or blocking plans and codes) is not built yet, so the SME supplies this.
policy.why: A grant or approval is stronger when an adopted plan already calls for the change. The area plan for this block is the 2022 Bowie-Mitchellville and Vicinity Master Plan, which the 2024 rezoning implements.
policy.ask: Which adopted plan or policy supports {thing} on {street}, and where (chapter, strategy or page)?

ref.label: 2022 Approved Bowie-Mitchellville and Vicinity Master Plan (M-NCPPC)

parcel.label: Parcel lookup
parcel.note: County parcel records (owner and site) are not connected yet, so the SME supplies this.
parcel.why: Who owns the land decides who acts: the City can only start work on land it controls, and private owners have to agree to anything on theirs.
parcel.ask: Who owns the parcels along {street} that this would touch: the City, M-NCPPC, another public agency, or private owners?

ref.label: Maryland SDAT real property records (owner of record per parcel)

road_owner.label: Road-owner lookup
road_owner.note: Whether the road is State (MD SHA), County or City is not looked up yet, so the SME supplies this.
road_owner.why: The road owner approves and permits anything in the right-of-way. On a state route that is MD SHA, which adds its own studies and access permits.
road_owner.ask: Who owns {street}: the State (MD SHA), Prince George's County or the City of Bowie?

ref.label: Road ownership: MD SHA, Prince George's County DPW&T or City of Bowie records

program_terms.label: Program-terms lookup
program_terms.note: The funding program's post-award rules are not extracted yet, so the SME supplies this.
program_terms.why: An award usually comes with conditions, such as matching funds, design approval or construction deadlines, and reporting, which set the timing of the later steps.
program_terms.ask: What does the chosen funding program require after award (match, deadlines for design and construction, reporting)?

ref.label: The chosen program's notice of funding or award agreement

pathways.name: Building and façade
pathways.branch: Is the condition a code violation the City can enforce, or an improvement beyond code that needs an incentive?

steps.title: Identify the property owners on the block
Decide the path: code violation or voluntary improvement
Inspect and issue a notice of violation; owner corrects
Find incentives: façade grant or loan, storefront program
Meet the owners; each decides whether to take part
Apply for the chosen program (the City or the owner, per program rules)
Design review of the façade change, if design rules apply
Building or sign permit
Work done and inspected; incentive paid on completion

pathways.name: Land use and development
pathways.branch: Is the use allowed by right, by special exception, or not at all without rezoning? Reductions mostly happen when a site redevelops.

steps.title: Look up the zone of each parcel on the block
Check whether the use is allowed: by right, special exception, or not allowed
Check what the area master plan says for the site
If not allowed by right: special exception hearing, or rezoning / text amendment
steps.owner: Zoning Hearing Examiner or District Council (confirm)

steps.title: Test the market: a willing owner or developer, and demand
Line up incentives to close any financing gap (tax credits, state programs)
Developer applies for site plan approval
Permits: building and stormwater, plus a state access permit on state routes
Construction

pathways.name: Parks and public space
pathways.branch: Is the site City land, county parkland (M-NCPPC) or private land? Is it construction, or programming like a farmers market?

steps.title: Pick a site and confirm who controls it
Secure the site: purchase, lease or easement
Check zoning allows park use on the parcel
Collect policy to cite: parks plan, master plan, health goals
Community input on the concept
Concept design and cost estimate
Apply for state or federal parks grants
If awarded: council accepts the grant; notify the planning committee
Final design approval, within the program's deadline
Permits: site, grading, stormwater
Bid and award the construction contract
Build, then grant close-out and a maintenance plan

pathways.name: Traffic control and crossings
pathways.branch: Is the road state (MD SHA), county or City? Signs and markings move fast; signals need a warrant study and take much longer.

steps.title: Confirm who owns the road
Request an engineering study: a crossing study, or a warrant analysis for signals and stop signs
Road owner approves the treatment
Find funding: maintenance budget for markings, grants for signals
Agreement or permit, if the City pays for or builds on a road it doesn't own
Design to the Maryland MUTCD
Install
steps.time: Weeks for markings; 3–6 mo for signals

steps.title: Agree who maintains it

pathways.name: Streetscape and sidewalks
pathways.branch: Who owns the road? Is the item capital work, a furnishing, a service an operator runs (bus stops, bike share), or a business permit (outdoor dining)?

steps.title: Confirm the road owner and the space available in the right-of-way
Collect policy to cite: complete streets, bike and pedestrian plans
Get into a capital budget, or a small-works budget for furnishings
Apply for transportation or streetscape grants
If awarded: council accepts; federal money adds environmental review
steps.owner: City Council; MD SHA for federal aid

steps.title: Design, utility coordination and ADA compliance
Permits: right-of-way permit; street trees may need a state roadside tree permit
Bid and build
Agree who maintains benches, trees and lights

pathways.name: Road and curb changes
pathways.branch: Who owns the road? Lane reductions need traffic analysis and public engagement; driveway reductions usually wait for redevelopment.

steps.title: Confirm who owns the road
Traffic and parking study: volumes for lane cuts; width and sight lines for parking
Collect policy to cite: complete streets, road diet guidance
Public engagement with businesses and residents
Road owner approves
Time it with scheduled resurfacing, or fund it separately
Striping and signing plan
Restripe and sign
Driveways: consolidate with owners, usually at redevelopment
steps.waits_on: Ties to land use and development
